findings.desc: Queue governance misclassifies valid worktree stories as stale when status commands run from a story worktree. projectQueueGovernance reads active stories from the current store/root, then worktreeIsStale resolves story.worktree.path relative to that same root (packages/main/src/core/lifecycle-control/queue/index.ts:200-205,317-323). For worktree invocations, story.worktree.path is main-root relative (for B-eb18, .worktrees/B-eb18), so the check probes /Users/jek/Documents/Work/proofbound/.worktrees/B-eb18/.worktrees/B-eb18 and falls into the catch/stale path. Observed command evidence: node packages/main/dist/cli.js global_control_status --storyIds=["B-eb18"] --format=json reports B-eb18 queue.classification="stale-worktree" / reason="authoritative worktree exists but appears stale/missing" even though the same report resolves authoritativeCwd=/Users/jek/Documents/Work/proofbound/.worktrees/B-eb18 and session_brief reports an active owner lease in that cwd. This breaks CP-3/CP-4 queue visibility by turning a valid authoritative worktree into cleanup-pressure noise; it does not appear to grant lifecycle readiness or Authority, so medium severity.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed queue worktree staleness to resolve recorded worktree paths through the canonical main repo root while preserving absolute paths. Verification passed: npm --prefix packages/main run build; node packages/main/dist/tasks/global-lifecycle-control-plane-smoke.js; npm --prefix packages/main run test:command-ownership-contract; npm --prefix packages/main run test:runtime-fact-contract.
